title: Golf ball, weight, cup

items.name: Wooden ramp
items.why: Wooden ramp from 55 cm down to 35 cm (about 18°). Its low end is in the air, so the ball flies off it

items.name: Golf ball
items.why: Waits near the top of the ramp until the release

items.name: Steel weight
items.why: An 8.6 cm steel cube pinned in place like a stop. The ball hits its left face in mid-flight and bounces back

items.name: Cup
items.why: Catches the ball as it drops back down in front of the weight

goals.label: The golf ball lands in the cup

notes: The ball leaves the ramp at about 1.7 m/s, 38 cm up. After about 0.13 s it hits the steel weight's left face about 23 cm above the table. The hard but poorly bouncing steel sends it back left at only about 0.6–0.8 m/s, so it falls almost straight down into the cup, 4–7 cm in front of the weight. The tuner can slide the cup to where the ball really drops.
assumptions: The steel weight is pinned in mid-air (as if bolted to a post) so it does not slide away when the ball hits it. A 5 kg weight was chosen so it is big enough to be hit reliably
The ramp's height and angle were chosen freely, since the request gave none
A standard 8 cm cup on the table, since no size was given
